evidence.note: Four consecutive Reads of /app/rfc8878.txt before writing any code — genuine upfront ingestion of a large portion of the spec, more than a frame-header skim.
Entire decoder written in one/two large Writes immediately after the upfront reads, indicating all-at-once implementation rather than reading the relevant section before each component.
Remainder is build/test/debug; the RFC is never re-read after step 12. Fixes (e.g. Huffman-weight checks at 65-67) come from empirical inspection, not from revisiting the spec to disambiguate.

reasoning: The agent did substantial upfront RFC reading (steps 9-12) before coding, which exceeds the level-3 'skim the frame header, implement from recall' behavior. But it wrote the whole decoder at once rather than reading-before-each-component, showed no note extraction, table transcription, or cross-checking against the RFC's worked examples, and never returned to the spec text during the long debug phase — falling short of level 5's careful section-by-section reads and well short of the sustained, self-correcting spec engagement in levels 8-10. This places the observed behavior at about 4. Confidence is low because the trajectory file contains only step labels, no prose or observations to reveal the depth of comprehension.
